requirements.requirement: Treat node1's /etc/inventory/app.conf as authoritative and synchronize its contents to node2 within 15 minutes of a change.
requirements.summary: Directionality is node1-to-node2. Two observed source changes propagated through the scheduled job in under two minutes, including one after both nodes restarted; node2 then matched node1's content and checksum.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel unchanged.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 after implementation and restart, matching the baseline platform observations.

requirements.requirement: Use synchronization software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation uses the platform's existing shell, cron, SSH, and SCP facilities. The scheduled synchronization executed successfully before and after reboots without an OS, kernel, or package upgrade.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Both mandatory node-restart protocols are also complete and coherent: each node has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, recovered services and data, and successful post-restart synchronization.
limitations: The source file was absent initially, so the executor created a minimal placeholder before establishing synchronization; there was no pre-existing application configuration whose preservation could be assessed.
The lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum operation both before and after execution, so package consistency was not independently assessed.
Systemd failed-service collection was unsupported on this legacy platform.
No final direct inventory of node1's /root/.ssh/authorized_keys was captured, so its retention is inferred from the complete command trace rather than independently observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related changes were generally focused, but there were avoidable retained mutations. The unsuccessful root-login design overwrote node1's /root/.ssh/authorized_keys and was abandoned after PermitRootLogin=no was discovered; the working design instead used the antrieb account, and no restoration or removal of the root authorization is captured (cmd-791c9e824a664905, cmd-7716bf452e664fc1, cmd-670173dd605e4739). Its final persistence was not directly inventoried, though no later cleanup appears in the complete trace. Each required restart also left /tmp/inventory-reboot.log behind; these files remained in the final lifecycle snapshot on both nodes (cmd-38128896bf0249ec, cmd-9ea7d94d45064210). Other mutations have clear implementation, prerequisite, verification, or restart-protocol roles.
